name: Lithuania
tagline: A baroque capital, a sand spit shared with Russia, and a hill of a hundred thousand crosses.
summary: Lithuania was once the largest state in Europe, and the memory of it sits oddly on a country of under three million. Vilnius has the biggest baroque old town in the region, full of courtyards you walk into by accident. The Curonian Spit is a 98-kilometre dune of shifting sand, and the Hill of Crosses is one of the strangest and most moving places on the continent.

season.note: Summer for the coast and the long evenings. September is warm, cheap and empty. Vilnius is at its best in the first week of March, when the Kaziukas craft fair takes over the old town.

getting_around: Vilnius, Kaunas and Klaipėda are linked by frequent buses; the coast needs a ferry from Klaipėda to the spit. The old town is entirely walkable and mostly cobbled.
food: Cepelinai: potato dumplings the size and shape of a zeppelin
Cold beetroot soup, shocking pink, served with a hot potato
Dark rye bread with garlic, fried, eaten with beer
know: The Hill of Crosses is an active devotional site, not a photo opportunity — leave one or leave it alone.
Užupis, in Vilnius, declared itself a republic in 1997 and has a constitution on a wall in twenty languages.
The Curonian Spit is shared with the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad; the border is real and closed to casual crossing.

regions.name: Vilnius & the East
regions.summary: The baroque capital, an artists' republic across a bridge, and a lake castle an hour away.

cities.name: Vilnius
cities.summary: Forty churches, endless courtyards, and a self-declared republic of artists over the river.
highlights: St Anne's, which Napoleon reportedly wanted to carry to Paris
The Gate of Dawn and its silver icon, still a pilgrimage
Užupis, its constitution and its angel
The KGB museum in the building where it happened

experiences.name: The courtyards nobody signposts
experiences.summary: The old town's real geography is behind the street doors; push the unlocked ones and keep going.

experiences.name: Read the Užupis constitution
experiences.summary: Forty-one articles on mirrored plaques, including a dog's right to be a dog and everyone's right to be happy — and not to be.

cities.name: Trakai
cities.summary: A red brick island castle in a lake, and the Karaim community that has lived beside it since the 14th century.
highlights: The island castle, reachable by footbridge
Kibinai pastries in Karaim wooden houses
Rowing boats and swimming in the same lake

regions.name: The Coast & Centre
regions.summary: The Curonian dunes, the port at Klaipėda, and the hill outside Šiauliai.

cities.name: Nida, Curonian Spit
cities.summary: Wooden fishermen's houses under a moving dune, on a sand spit between lagoon and sea.
highlights: Parnidis dune and its sundial, with the Russian border visible south
Thomas Mann's summer house, where he wrote in 1930–32
Amber, smoked fish, and no cars to speak of

experiences.name: The grey dunes at first light
experiences.summary: Sand that buried four villages in the 19th century; the boardwalk exists because walking on it directly would start it moving again.

cities.name: Šiauliai
cities.summary: An industrial town whose reason to visit stands in a field twelve kilometres north.
highlights: The Hill of Crosses: over 100,000 crosses, bulldozed three times by the Soviets and rebuilt each night
The sound the small crosses make in wind
A cathedral with a sundial column

experiences.name: The Hill of Crosses
experiences.summary: Not a monument — an act repeated by hundreds of thousands of people, most of them anonymous, over two centuries.
